title: Multipart upload: a failed part costs one part, not the whole file
caption: Parts go in parallel and in any order; nothing is visible under the key until complete stitches them by part number.

messages.label: initiate upload clip.mp4
messages.note: The store returns an uploadId that ties the parts together.

messages.label: PUT part 3 (64 MB)
messages.note: Parts are separate requests, so several connections run at once.

messages.label: PUT part 2 (64 MB)
messages.note: The connection drops mid-part. Only these 64 MB are lost.

messages.label: retry PUT part 2
messages.note: Retry just this part. Each success returns an ETag for it.

messages.label: complete [1:e1, 2:e2, 3:e3]
messages.note: The client lists part numbers and ETags; the store assembles in part order, not arrival order.

messages.label: 200 · object visible
messages.note: Atomic: readers see the whole object or nothing. Abandoned uploads are cleaned up by a lifecycle rule.

scenarios.name: Alternative: one big PUT
scenarios.summary: A single PUT is simpler, but a drop at 90% throws away 3.6 GB and the retry starts from byte 0. Fine for small files; use multipart above ~100 MB.

messages.label: PUT clip.mp4 (4 GB)
messages.note: One request on one connection at ~100 MB/s: about 40 s on a fast link, many minutes on a phone.

messages.label: … 3.6 GB sent, connection drops
messages.note: A PUT is all or nothing: the store keeps none of it.

messages.label: PUT clip.mp4 again (4 GB)
messages.note: The retry re-sends every byte, and on a flaky link it can drop again.

messages.label: 200 · object visible
messages.note: It works eventually, after paying for the whole file twice or more.

scenarios.name: Abandoned upload
scenarios.summary: The app is killed after 40 of 64 parts: the object never appears, but its parts are stored and billed until the upload is aborted, so add a lifecycle rule that does it.

messages.label: PUT parts 1–40 (2.5 GB)
messages.note: Parts go up in parallel as usual.

messages.label: app killed, no complete
messages.note: The user swipes the app away. Nothing ever calls complete or abort.

messages.label: 40 parts kept, billed
messages.note: Nothing is visible under the key and a normal LIST doesn't show them, but the bytes cost storage like any object. Millions of these add up.

messages.label: lifecycle: abort after 7 d
messages.note: Mitigation: a bucket rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads after N days and frees their parts.

scenarios.name: Too many parts
scenarios.summary: Stores cap an upload at about 10,000 parts. A 100 GB file in 5 MB parts would need 20,000, so pick the part size from the file size.

messages.label: PUT parts 1–10,000 (5 MB each)
messages.note: Small parts retry cheaply, but 10,000 × 5 MB only covers 50 GB.

messages.label: 400 · part number too large
messages.note: Fix: part size = max(8 MB, file size ÷ 10,000). For 100 GB that's ~11 MB parts, so the upload fits in under 10,000.
